The '''2017–18 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team''' represented [[Clemson University]] during the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. Led by eighth-year head coach [[Brad Brownell]], the Tigers played their home games at [[Littlejohn Coliseum]] in [[Clemson, South Carolina]] as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. They finished the season 25–10, 11–7 in [[2017–18 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in four-way tie for third place. They defeated [[2017–18 Boston College Eagles men's basketball team|Boston College]] in the quarterfinals of the [[2018 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] before losing in the semifinals to [[2017–18 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they defeated [[2017–18 New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball team|New Mexico State]] and [[2017–18 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]] to advance to the Sweet Sixteen where they lost to [[2017–18 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]]. The Tigers 25 wins tied the most in program history and their 11 conference wins were the most in program history at the time.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.clemsontigers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=657841&SPID=103715&DB_OEM_ID=28500&ATCLID=211707552|title=Clemson's Season Still Sweet Despite 80-76 loss to Kansas|website=clemsontigers.com|publisher=Clemson University Athletic Department|date=March 23, 2018|accessdate=March 26, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180326203144/http://www.clemsontigers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=657841&SPID=103715&DB_OEM_ID=28500&ATCLID=211707552|archive-date=March 26, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Previous season==
The [[2016–17 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Tigers]] finished the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17 season]] 17–16, 6–12 in [[2016–17 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in 12th place. They lost in the second round of the [[2017 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] to [[2016–17 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]]. They received an invitation to the [[2017 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitation Tournament]] where they lost in the first round to [[2016–17 Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball team|Oakland]].

== Offseason ==
On June 19, 2017, the Tigers announced the signing of [[Antonio Reynolds-Dean]] as an assistant coach.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tigernet.com/update/Dean-named-Clemson-Assistant-Men%E2%80%99s-Basketball-Coach-27039?ref=fb|title=Dean named Clemson Assistant Men's Basketball Coach|date=June 19, 2017|website=TigerNet.com|publisher=Tigernet.com|access-date=June 19, 2017}}</ref> Dean replaces longtime assistant Mike Winiecki, who left the program in April.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://sports.usatoday.com/2017/06/19/reynolds-dean-named-clemson-assistant-basketball-coach/|title=Reynolds Dean named Clemson assistant basketball coach|date=2017-06-19|website=USA TODAY Sports|access-date=2017-06-26}}</ref>
